title: Direction & Distance
source: MindSpark Grade 7 Aptitude & Reasoning | Chapter 3: Direction & Distance
subtopics: 8 Compass Directions (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW)
Turning Left and Right — 90° and 180° Turns
Final Position and Direction After Turns
Shortest Distance Between Two Points on a Path
Speed Round: Mixed Direction & Distance Problems
learningGoals: Track a person's position and direction accurately through multi-step movement descriptions.
Apply the Pythagorean theorem to find the straight-line (shortest) distance from start to end.
Determine the final facing direction after a sequence of left and right turns.
coreIdeas: Always draw the path on paper — mark North at the top, label each segment with distance and direction.
For shortest distance: separate total horizontal movement (East–West net) and vertical movement (North–South net), then use a²+b²=c².
Right turn = clockwise 90°. Left turn = anti-clockwise 90°. Two right turns = 180° = about-face.

workedExamples.problem: Ravi starts facing North, walks 5 km North, turns right and walks 4 km East. How far is he from the start?
workedExamples.solution: Draw the path: 5 km up (North), 4 km right (East). This forms a right-angle triangle. Distance = √(5²+4²) = √(25+16) = √41 ≈ 6.4 km.
workedExamples.concept: Pythagoras for shortest distance after two perpendicular legs

workedExamples.problem: A man faces East. He turns left twice. Which direction is he now facing?
workedExamples.solution: Starting direction: East. Left turn 1 (anti-clockwise 90°): North. Left turn 2: West. Final direction: West.
workedExamples.concept: Turning left/right changes the facing direction by 90° per turn

workedExamples.problem: Meera walks 3 km North, then 4 km East, then 3 km South. What is her displacement from the start?
workedExamples.solution: North–South: +3 (North) then -3 (South) = net 0 km. East–West: +4 (East) = net 4 km East. Displacement = 4 km East from start.
workedExamples.concept: Net displacement — opposite directions cancel each other out

onboarding.coachIntro: Spark checks if the student knows all 4 cardinal directions and can name which way is 'right' when facing North. Warm-up draws a compass rose.
onboarding.placementRule: Start at Group A. Students struggling with N/S/E/W see a compass orientation exercise before Group A begins.

mission.missionPromise: By the end you will trace any multi-step path, calculate the shortest distance using Pythagoras, and identify final facing direction — 3 guaranteed marks in aptitude exams!
mission.successCelebration: Award a 'Navigator' badge after each group. Final trophy: 'Direction Maze Master'.

microLessonPattern: Coach draws a compass rose and labels all 8 directions at lesson start.
Coach traces the path step by step on the board, labelling each segment.
Coach applies Pythagoras on the right-triangle formed by the path.
Student traces the path independently and states the final position.
Instant feedback confirms both the distance AND the final facing direction.
Review prompt asks student to name the direction 90° clockwise from the current facing direction.

beats.teacherLine: Direction & Distance is your GPS skill! Every problem has a person moving through steps — North, South, East, West, turning left or right. Your job: track their position and find how far they ended up from where they started. Two tools make this easy: a hand-drawn path diagram and Pythagoras for the final distance. Let me show you both!
beats.boardAction: Draw a large compass rose with all 8 directions labelled. Write the 3 steps: (1) Draw the path with arrows and distances. (2) Find net horizontal and vertical displacement. (3) Apply Pythagoras if the path forms a right angle.
beats.checkpointPrompt: If you are facing North and turn right, which direction are you now facing?
beats.fallbackHint: Imagine standing and looking North (up). Turning right means rotating clockwise. The next direction clockwise from North is East.

svgAnimation.text: Step 2: Find net N-S and net E-W displacement

beats.teacherLine: Watch me solve live: 'Ravi walks 5 km North, turns right, walks 4 km East. How far from start?' Step 1: Draw arrow 5 units up, then 4 units right — an L-shape. Step 2: Net North = 5, Net East = 4. Step 3: Distance = √(5²+4²) = √(25+16) = √41. But many exam answers are clean numbers — check if it is a 3-4-5 or 5-12-13 Pythagorean triple first!
beats.boardAction: Draw the L-shape path: 5 km North then 4 km East. Mark start as S and end as E. Draw the hypotenuse dashed line. Label: a=5, b=4, c=√41. Write Pythagorean triples: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17.
beats.checkpointPrompt: If someone walks 3 km North and 4 km East, how far from the start? (Hint: 3-4-5 triple!)
beats.fallbackHint: 3 and 4 are the two short sides. In the 3-4-5 Pythagorean triple, the hypotenuse is 5. Distance = 5 km. No calculator needed — memorise the triple!

beats.teacherLine: You now have all the tools: compass drawing, turning rules, and Pythagoras. For Groups A–H, always draw the path before answering. Memorise these Pythagorean triples — they appear constantly: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17, 7-24-25. If you see those numbers in a distance problem, the answer is clean!
beats.boardAction: Write the 4 Pythagorean triples in a box. Write turn rules: Facing N → right turn → E → right turn → S → right turn → W → right turn → N (full circle). Anti-clockwise is the same cycle reversed.
beats.checkpointPrompt: If a person faces West and makes 3 right turns, which direction are they facing?
beats.fallbackHint: West → right turn → North → right turn → East → right turn → South. Three right turns from West = South? Wait — let me recount: West+90°CW = North, North+90°CW = East, East+90°CW = South. Three rights from West = South.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Eight directions on a compass — N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW. Know them all by heart and you save 5 seconds every question!

boardDemo.title: 8 Compass Directions — Clockwise Order
steps: Clockwise from North: N → NE → E → SE → S → SW → W → NW → N
Opposite pairs: N↔S, E↔W, NE↔SW, NW↔SE
45° between adjacent directions
Mnemonic: Never Eat Soggy Waffles = N,E,S,W
boardDemo.teacherLine: Memorise the clockwise order of all 8 directions. Every turn problem uses this order. Opposite direction is always 4 steps away in the clockwise ring.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Going clockwise: after South-East (SE), what is the next direction?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Name the direction that is exactly opposite to North-West (NW).
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! NW and SE are exact opposites (4 steps apart clockwise). Compass locked in!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: NW is in the top-left. Its opposite is in the bottom-right — that is SE (South-East).
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: list all 8 directions in clockwise order starting from North.

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise B: Left and Right Turns
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Turn right = rotate clockwise 90°. Turn left = anti-clockwise 90°. Simple rule, but easy to get mixed up — let's nail it!

boardDemo.title: 90° Turns — Clockwise and Anti-clockwise
steps: Facing North, turn right (CW) → now facing East
Facing East, turn right (CW) → now facing South
Facing North, turn left (CCW) → now facing West
Facing South, turn 180° (about-face) → now facing North
boardDemo.teacherLine: Right turn always goes to the next direction clockwise. Left turn goes to the next direction anti-clockwise. Practice the ring: N→E→S→W→N going right.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: A person faces South and turns right. Which direction are they now facing?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: A person faces East, turns left, then turns left again. Which direction are they facing now?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Perfect! East → left → North → left → West. Two left turns from East = West. Turn logic mastered!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: East → left turn → North (CCW from E is N). North → left turn → West. Two lefts from East = West.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: starting facing North, after 3 right turns, which direction do you face?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Multiple steps, multiple turns — draw every single arrow. Your diagram is the answer, the numbers just fill in the details.

boardDemo.title: Multi-Step Path — Draw Every Leg
steps: Problem: Walk 4 km N, turn right, walk 3 km E, turn right, walk 4 km S
Draw leg 1: 4 km up. Leg 2: 3 km right. Leg 3: 4 km down.
Final position: 3 km East of start (North and South cancel)
Distance from start = 3 km
boardDemo.teacherLine: When North and South legs are equal, they cancel perfectly. Same for East and West. Always compute net displacement on each axis before applying Pythagoras.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Path: 6 km North, 6 km South. What is the net North-South displacement?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Full path: 5 km North, 5 km East, 5 km South. What is the shortest distance from the start? Draw it!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! North and South cancel (5-5=0). Net displacement = 5 km East. Distance from start = 5 km. Clean answer — no Pythagoras needed!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: 5 km N then 5 km S — those cancel: net N-S = 0. Remaining: 5 km E. The person is just 5 km East of start.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Practice: 3 km N, 4 km E, 3 km N, 4 km W. How far and in what direction from start?

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise D: Shortest Distance Using Pythagoras
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! When your path makes an L-shape, Pythagoras gives you the straight-line shortcut home. a²+b²=c² — the most powerful tool in direction problems!

boardDemo.title: Pythagoras in Direction Problems
steps: L-shaped path: a km in one direction, b km perpendicular
The start, turn point, and end form a right triangle
Hypotenuse c = √(a² + b²)
Check for Pythagorean triples first: 3-4-5, 5-12-13, 8-15-17
boardDemo.teacherLine: The Pythagorean triple check saves time in exams. See 3 and 4? Answer is 5. See 5 and 12? Answer is 13. Recognise the triple instantly.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: A girl walks 12 km East then 5 km North. What is the straight-line distance back to start?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: A boy walks 8 km West then 15 km North. What is the shortest distance from his starting point?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Outstanding! 8 and 15 — that is the 8-15-17 Pythagorean triple! Distance = 17 km. You recognised the triple instantly — that is exam speed!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: 8²+15² = 64+225 = 289. √289 = 17. Distance = 17 km. Remember the 8-15-17 triple!
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: someone walks 7 km South and 24 km East. What is the shortest distance from start?

sessionFlow.subtopic: Final Position and Direction After Turns
sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise E: Final Position After Multiple Turns
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Track both WHERE the person is AND which way they are facing at the end. Two answers needed — position and facing direction.

boardDemo.title: Position + Final Facing Direction
steps: Problem: Start facing North. Walk 4 km N. Turn right. Walk 3 km E. Turn right. Walk 2 km S.
After all moves: 2 km North and 3 km East of start
Facing direction: started N, turned right (→E), turned right again (→S)
Final facing: South
boardDemo.teacherLine: Track the facing direction separately from the position. Each right turn adds one step clockwise in the direction ring. Count the total turns to find final facing.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: A person starts facing East, walks 3 km, turns left, walks 4 km, turns right. What direction are they now facing?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Start facing North. Walk 5 km North, turn left, walk 3 km West, turn right. (1) Final facing direction? (2) How far from start?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Correct! Turns: N → left (W) → right (N). Final facing = North. Position: 5N-3W, distance = √(25+9) = √34 ≈ 5.8 km. Both answers — full marks!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: track turns separately. Start N, turn left = face W, turn right = face N again. For distance: 5 km N and 3 km W form a right triangle: √(5²+3²)=√34.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: start facing South, turn right twice, walk 5 km, turn left. What direction are you facing?

sessionFlow.subtopic: Shortest Distance Between Two Points on a Path
sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise F: Shortest Path Between Two Points
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Sometimes you need the distance between the person's current position and a specific point they passed earlier — not the start!

boardDemo.title: Distance Between Mid-Path Points
steps: Problem: Walk 6 km N (Point A), then 8 km E (Point B), then 6 km S (Point C).
Distance from A to C? A is at (0,6) relative to start, C is at (8,0) relative to start.
Horizontal diff: 8, Vertical diff: 6. Distance AC = √(8²+6²) = √(64+36) = √100 = 10 km.
boardDemo.teacherLine: Mark coordinates for each point in your diagram. Use (East, North) as (x, y). Distance between two points = √((x2-x1)² + (y2-y1)²).

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: A man walks 3 km East to Point A, then 4 km North to Point B. What is the direct distance from his start to Point B?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: A woman walks 9 km East, then 12 km North. What is the straight-line distance from her start to her current position?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Brilliant! 9 and 12 — that is a 9-12-15 triple (multiple of 3-4-5). Distance = 15 km. Recognised the triple: 3×(3-4-5) = 9-12-15. Pro move!
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Practice: walk 5 km North to A, then 12 km East to B, then 5 km South to C. Distance from A to C?

sessionFlow.missionStepTitle: Exercise G: Facing Direction After Many Turns
sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code! Long chains of turns — 5, 6, even 8 turns. Instead of tracing each one, use modular arithmetic: 4 right turns = full circle = back to start!

boardDemo.title: Modular Turn Counting — 4 Turns = Full Cycle
steps: 4 right turns = full 360° = same direction as start
Count net right turns: subtract left turns from right turns
Net 1 right = 90° CW, net 2 right = 180° (opposite), net 3 right = 270° CW (=90° CCW)
Example: 5 right turns − 1 left turn = 4 net rights = back to start direction
boardDemo.teacherLine: Divide the net number of right turns by 4 — only the remainder matters! Remainder 0 = same direction. Remainder 1 = 90° CW. Remainder 2 = 180° flip. Remainder 3 = 90° CCW.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Starting facing East: 6 right turns and 2 left turns. Net right turns = 4. What direction are you facing?
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Start facing North: 7 right turns, 3 left turns. Net rights = 4. Remainder = 0. What is the final facing direction?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Spot on! Net 4 rights = full circle = back to North. Modular turn counting wins! You just solved 10 turns in 3 seconds.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: 7 right - 3 left = 4 net right turns. 4 right turns = 360° = full circle. You end facing the same direction you started: North.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Quick: start facing West, 9 right turns, 5 left turns. Net = 4. Final direction?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let's crack this code — FAST! Mixed direction and distance problems at Olympiad pace. Draw fast, calculate fast, state both position and facing direction!

boardDemo.title: Speed Checklist — 3 Questions in 90 Seconds
steps: Step 1: Draw path immediately (no hesitation)
Step 2: Cancel opposite-direction legs
Step 3: Check for Pythagorean triples before using √
Step 4: Count net turns (mod 4) for facing direction
Goal: under 30 seconds per question
boardDemo.teacherLine: Olympiad direction questions always have clean answers — Pythagorean triples or exact cancellations. If your answer looks messy (like √41), check your diagram before committing.

sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Ready for the speed round? 3 questions coming. State the distance AND the final facing direction.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: Q1: Walk 15 km N, 20 km E — distance from start? | Q2: Face S, turn right 3 times — facing direction? | Q3: Walk 6 N, 8 E, 6 S — distance from start?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: INCREDIBLE! Q1: 15-20-25 triple (5×3-4-5). Q2: S+3 rights = S→W→N→E = East. Wait — S,W,N,E: 3 rights from S = East. Q3: N and S cancel, net 8 km East = 8 km. Direction Maze fully navigated!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Here's a trick: Q1: 15=5×3, 20=5×4 → hypotenuse=5×5=25. Q2: S→right→W→right→N→right→E, so 3 rights from S = East. Q3: 6N and 6S cancel, only 8E remains.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Final recap: state the three steps for solving any direction and distance problem.
